title: Such prophetic doubt is infirmity to fight, not virtue to imitate; make calling sure by good works
source_text: XX. Verum in sanctis illis viris id fuit magnum humanae infirmitatis argumentum, non autem opus virtutis imitandum. Itaque si qua talis fidelium animis occurrat dubitatio, minime fovenda est, sub humilitatis praetextu; sed omnibus modis impugnanda & expellenda, per assiduam verbi Dei meditationem, per seria & ferventia vota, & per sanctitatis studium. Juxta quod monet Petrus Apostolus, dum vult nos satagere ut per bona opera nostram vocationem & electionem certam faciamus. 2 Pet. 1.
pass_a_gloss: But in those holy men that was a great argument of human infirmity, not a work of virtue to be imitated. And so if any such doubt occurs in believers’ minds, it is by no means to be fostered under pretext of humility; but is to be attacked and expelled by every means—by assiduous meditation on God’s word, by serious and fervent prayers, and by the pursuit of holiness. According to what Peter the Apostle advises when he wants us to be diligent that by good works we make our calling and election sure (2 Pet. 1).
pass_b_english: Prophetic doubt is weakness to resist, not humility to cultivate.
Fight it by Word, prayer, and holiness, making calling sure by good works.
